messages:
kevin: Heads-up — ACME reported that calls to their private service endpoint `svc.internal.acme` from our Private deployment in their VPC are failing with NXDOMAIN. They said this started after they imported a bunch of hosted zones this morning. App-level error: 502 gateway / connect error.

marta: thanks. can you paste the `dig` output and which VPC/subnet this happens from? also any recent resolver rule changes on their side?

kevin: Repro from one of our worker nodes in their VPC (10.1.12.7):
```
$ dig @172.31.0.2 svc.internal.acme +short

# empty -> NXDOMAIN answer observed in the full output
$ dig svc.internal.acme
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.13-Ubuntu <<>> svc.internal.acme
;; global options: +cmd
;; Got answer:
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
internal.acme. 300 IN SOA ns-1.acme.internal. root.acme.internal. 1 7200 900 1209600 300
```

kevin: curl error: `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: svc.internal.acme` from the same node.

sasha: do we see any resolver-rule associations or private hosted zones that shadow that name? can you run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name internal.acme` and `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=Status,Values=ACTIVE` from their account (or ask customer to paste)?

acme-appops: pasted outputs:
```
# route53 hosted zones (their account):
{ "HostedZones": [ { "Id": "/hostedzone/Z123ABC", "Name": "internal.acme.", "Config": { "PrivateZone": true } } ] }
# resolver rule associations (their account):
{ "ResolverRuleAssociations": [ { "Id": "rra-abc123", "Name": "forward-to-onprem", "Status": "COMPLETE", "VPCId": "vpc-0a1b2c3d" } ] }
```

marta: interesting — they do have a private hosted zone `internal.acme.` associated to the same VPC. that will create a split-horizon for any name under internal.acme. if the hosted zone has no record for `svc` it will NXDOMAIN instead of forwarding to the expected resolver. do we know if `svc.internal.acme` should be managed by their hosted zone or expected to resolve to a service endpoint (eg a cross-account private endpoint)?

acme-appops: we created the hosted zone to manage some internal names but we expected the service endpoint records to be created automatically by the service (they thought it was a shared private hosted zone owned by the vendor). we didn't add `svc` records.

sasha: that matches the symptom. two ways to fix: (A) add the missing A/CNAME records for `svc.internal.acme` in their private hosted zone pointing to the service endpoint IP/CNAME, or (B) remove/disassociate their private hosted zone from the VPC so the DNS will fall back to the original owner (if that's the intended behavior).

kevin: we also saw this oddity — node-local DNS cache returning stale NXDOMAIN even after they added records. steps we recommended to them to flush: restart node-local-dns pods (or `systemctl restart systemd-resolved` on VMs), or incrementally reduce cache TTL. they restarted node-local-dns and it cleared.

marta: quick checklist we ran with them: 
- confirmed private hosted zone present and associated -> yes
- checked zone records -> `svc` missing -> yes
- ensured outbound 53/udp to Amazon resolver allowed -> allowed (security groups/NACLs ok)
- validated resolver-rule priority (local zone takes precedence) -> confirmed

kevin: small wrinkle — they also have an explicit Route53 Resolver rule forwarding `*.acme.external` to an on-prem resolver which is NOT used for `internal.acme` but worth noting. forwarding rules can interact with private zones if names overlap.

acme-appops: we disassociated the private hosted zone from the VPC (we wanted the vendor-managed records), restarted node-local-dns, and now `dig svc.internal.acme +short` returns the expected CNAME -> svc.vendor.internal.edge and curl works.

sasha: great. root cause summary: customer-created private hosted zone `internal.acme` in their account shadowed vendor-managed records for `svc.internal.acme` and since `svc` didn't exist in the zone it returned NXDOMAIN. resolution was to either add the records in the zone or remove the association so the vendor-owned zone can respond. also reminded them about node-local cache needing a restart to observe the change quickly.

marta: adding notes for support KB: 1) shadowing from private hosted zones is a common cause for private endpoint NXDOMAIN; 2) check both hosted zones + resolver rules + node-local caching; 3) verify SG/NACL egress for UDP/TCP 53 and Route53 resolver endpoints if forwarding.

eng-oncall-bot: Incident ticket #INC-2026 created and linked to customer case 99822.

kevin: closing the loop with ACME. they asked if we can detect this automatically — suggested we add a diagnostic in our private deployer that warns when customer private hosted zones intersect typical service endpoint namespaces.

acme-appops: thanks team :thumbsup:
